narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the purpose of the loan, and the length of time you have lived at your current residence. 

The requested amount of 2,528 DM was the most important factor and worked in your favor by pushing the prediction toward good credit. It is noticeably lower than the average amount approved applicants request. Unfortunately, this positive effect was outweighed by the other two key factors. 

The fact that the loan is intended for business purposes was the second most influential element and pulled the prediction toward bad credit risk. Only 8.7% of approved applicants use loans for business, whereas most approved loans are for radio/TV or furniture.

Finally, having lived at your present address for just one year was the third strongest driver and also increased the estimated risk. Approved applicants have typically lived at their current home almost three years on average.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude your application carried too much risk. You should focus on building a longer track record at your current address and consider applying again in the future with a non-business purpose or after you have accumulated more savings. Reviewing your credit history and exploring smaller loan amounts may also improve your prospects next time. (248 words)
